scope: Geographical requirements use primary territory, excluding overseas regions and dependencies (France means metropolitan France). Statistical comparisons use the World Bank’s reporting territory and 2023 data. Capital points are fixed to the demo’s 2023 convention: Jakarta for Indonesia and Pretoria for South Africa. Historical and cultural requirements state their own date range. Tap any requirement for its exact definition.

attributes.label: In Africa
attributes.definition: Has land in Africa in its primary geographical territory. Transcontinental countries qualify. Overseas regions and dependencies are excluded.

attributes.label: Crosses the equator
attributes.definition: The equator crosses land in the country’s primary geographical territory, not merely its territorial waters.

attributes.label: Landlocked
attributes.definition: The country has no coastline on an ocean or a sea connected to an ocean. Lakes do not count as a coast.

attributes.label: Portuguese is official
attributes.definition: Portuguese is an official language at national level, not simply a widely spoken or regional language.

attributes.label: Drives on the left
attributes.definition: Normal road traffic keeps to the left side of the road.

attributes.label: Southern Hemisphere
attributes.definition: Some land in the country’s primary geographical territory lies south of the equator. Overseas regions and dependencies are excluded; France means metropolitan France.

attributes.label: In Europe
attributes.definition: Has land in Europe in its primary geographical territory. Transcontinental countries qualify. Overseas regions and dependencies are excluded.

attributes.label: Uses the euro
attributes.definition: The euro is the country’s official national currency, not merely accepted by some businesses.

attributes.label: In Asia
attributes.definition: Has land in Asia in its primary geographical territory. Transcontinental countries qualify. Overseas regions and dependencies are excluded.

attributes.label: Atlantic coastline
attributes.definition: The primary geographical territory has a coast on the Atlantic Ocean, including the Gulf of Guinea. The Mediterranean Sea is excluded.

attributes.label: Mediterranean coast
attributes.definition: The primary geographical territory has a coast directly on the Mediterranean Sea.

attributes.label: GDP greater than Austria’s
attributes.definition: Total nominal GDP in current US dollars, not GDP per person or purchasing-power parity. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: More people than Japan
attributes.definition: Total resident population, not the population of the capital. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: Fewer people than Australia
attributes.definition: Total resident population, not population density. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: Smaller than Japan
attributes.definition: Surface area including inland water, measured in square kilometres. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: Larger than India
attributes.definition: Surface area including inland water, measured in square kilometres. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: More people than Germany
attributes.definition: Total resident population. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: GDP per person above Portugal’s
attributes.definition: Nominal GDP divided by population, in current US dollars. This is an economic average, not personal income. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: More densely populated than Germany
attributes.definition: Population divided by total surface area, including inland water. This differs from measures that use land area only. Uses World Bank 2023 figures for both countries, with strict comparisons on unrounded data. Statistical reporting territories may include overseas territory.

attributes.label: Capital within 2,000 miles of Cairo
attributes.definition: The fixed capital point is no more than 2,000 statute miles from Cairo, measured along a great circle on a spherical Earth (mean radius 3,958.7613 miles). This is city-to-city distance, not distance from the nearest border. Answers use unrounded distances. Capital points follow the demo’s 2023 convention, using Pretoria for South Africa and Jakarta for Indonesia.

attributes.label: Capital within 1,500 miles of Paris
attributes.definition: The fixed capital point is no more than 1,500 statute miles from Paris, measured along a great circle on a spherical Earth (mean radius 3,958.7613 miles). This is city-to-city distance, not distance from the nearest border. Answers use unrounded distances. Capital points follow the demo’s 2023 convention, using Pretoria for South Africa and Jakarta for Indonesia.

attributes.label: Capital within 3,500 miles of Tokyo
attributes.definition: The fixed capital point is no more than 3,500 statute miles from Tokyo, measured along a great circle on a spherical Earth (mean radius 3,958.7613 miles). This is city-to-city distance, not distance from the nearest border. Answers use unrounded distances. Capital points follow the demo’s 2023 convention, using Pretoria for South Africa and Jakarta for Indonesia.

attributes.label: Capital closer to Cairo than Paris
attributes.definition: Compare great-circle distances from the fixed capital point to Cairo and Paris. Cairo must be strictly closer; ties do not qualify. Uses the demo’s 2023 capital convention, with Pretoria for South Africa and Jakarta for Indonesia.

attributes.label: Capital closer to Tokyo than Paris
attributes.definition: Compare great-circle distances from the fixed capital point to Tokyo and Paris. Tokyo must be strictly closer; ties do not qualify. Uses the demo’s 2023 capital convention, with Pretoria for South Africa and Jakarta for Indonesia.

attributes.label: Has hosted the Summer Olympics
attributes.definition: Had a main host city for a Summer Olympic Games edition from 1896 through 2024 inclusive. Excludes cancelled editions, Youth Games, bids and satellite venues. Tokyo’s 2020 edition counts although held in 2021. West German hosts count for Germany.

attributes.label: Has hosted the Winter Olympics
attributes.definition: Had a main host city for a Winter Olympic Games edition from 1924 through 2024 inclusive. Excludes cancelled editions, Youth Games, bids and satellite venues. Later editions are outside this fixed snapshot.

attributes.label: Has won the men’s football World Cup
attributes.definition: Won the senior men’s FIFA World Cup at least once from 1930 through 2022 inclusive. West Germany’s titles count for Germany. Women’s, youth and club competitions are separate events.

attributes.label: UNESCO Mediterranean diet heritage
attributes.definition: Is a named participant in UNESCO’s shared Mediterranean diet inscription by the end of 2024. This is a specific cultural heritage record, not a judgement about national eating habits or whether the country borders the Mediterranean.

attributes.label: Autocratic rule in 1980
attributes.definition: Classified as a closed or electoral autocracy in 1980 by V-Dem’s Regimes of the World (v16), as processed by Our World in Data. This is a classification of political institutions, not whether a particular leader is called a dictator. Historical country units follow the dataset; missing records remain unknown.
